title: Verbal irony: Pretense or echoic mention?

verification.verification_notes: Metadata confirmed via Crossref API; volume/issue/pagination (113(1):130-136) confirmed 2026-09-24. The echoic-mention account holds that verbal irony echoes an actual or attributed thought while signalling a dissociated attitude toward it; irony is therefore interpretive rather than literal inversion. This is the mechanism by which bitter irony targets a stated ideal. Full text not re-inspected; no passage quoted.
